lead: Brent Crude / BZ=F — one push from the hundred-dollar barrel
smaller: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC — the stock outruns its stumbling app
SoFi Technologies / SOFI — a billion-dollar bet on one-stop banking
AMC Entertainment / AMC — meme veterans count scars in a correction
why_lead: The 22 February session turned the Russia threat into policy and the oil price into a round-number chase: Brent 96.84 USD/bbl, +3.53% from its 18 February close (the card has no 21 February Brent session, so the move spans the holiday) and +12.25% over 20 sessions, TTF gas +8.17% from 18 February, wheat +5.93%, with S&P 500 -1.01% and VIX 28.81. Newly published evidence: oil 'nearing $100' (NYT n1109, Guardian n1263, NPR n1264, BBC n1275), Germany freezing Nord Stream 2 (Reuters n1099, Guardian n1101), new US and UK sanctions (Al Jazeera n1255, with Biden's 'beginning invasion' framed as his characterisation; GOV.UK n1272), Sberbank/VTB rebounding as top banks escaped UK sanctions (n0764), consumer-facing coverage (LA Times n1274, Kiplinger n1605), the WSJ's US-near-Iran-deal report (n1245) qualified by Reuters' draft-puts-oil-later report (n1184), and Bloomberg's Covid-crash-to-$100 analog (n0082). Relation to earlier notes: oil appeared as a smaller USO item on 15 February (seven-year-high war barrel, producer non-confirmation, stalled Iran talks) and Exxon on 2 and 8 February (Nord Stream pledge, $100 strategist target). This is a material update: the Nord Stream halt and first sanctions are now facts rather than threats, the Iran valve has moved from stalled talks to a near-deal whose oil comes later, and the sanctions-are-narrow read (Sberbank rebound) is new; the producer non-confirmation recurs with new 22 February data. It is promoted to lead because it is the day's dominant crowd narrative, and DWAC, the 21 and 22 February lead, is demoted to a secondary item to avoid a third consecutive DWAC lead. No outcome after the cutoff (invasion, later sanctions, later prices) is used; the pending RBNZ, Lowe's, TJX, Lucid and eBay events are not referenced.
why_smaller: Digital World Acquisition: material update to the 21-22 February leads, kept secondary. New evidence is the first post-launch trading session (DWAC 92.90 USD, +10.18%, +38.22% 20s, on a down day for the S&P 500) and newly published coverage: Reuters on the SPAC's surge as Truth Social topped downloads (n0780), Apptopia's 170k downloads (n1604), The Week's 13-hour crash right after the Monday launch (n1609) and Bloomberg's Dubsmash story as the cautionary analog (n1603). The 22 February lead's test, holding above the pre-launch 84.32 USD at Tuesday's open, was passed. The title was corrected in review: the crash came on Monday, before Tuesday's surge, so 'the ticket paid, then the app crashed' had the order wrong. CNBC's chart-topping report (n1611) was dropped as a restatement of the 22 February ranking.

SoFi Technologies: a new, distinct fintech narrative not used in earlier notes. SOFI fell 9.92% to 10.26 USD (-22.86% 20s) on the day it agreed to buy Technisys for $1.1B (Banking Dive n0771, American Banker one-stop-shop n0769), with HOOD -15.28% and SQ -15.88% over five sessions and the 2Y at 1.56% (+57 bps 20 obs) as the break conditions. Earlier fintech items were PayPal (2 and 3 February) and Affirm (14 February).

AMC Entertainment: the meme crowd's endurance narrative, refreshed by new 22 February attention evidence (Time's 'I'm down 20 grand, but I'm still up' meme-trading retrospective n0675, WSJ+ GameStop/Reddit event n0739) and a -7.99% AMC session in a confirmed S&P 500 correction (Reuters n1924, CNBC n0711). Relation to earlier notes: GameStop led on 1 February and AMC was a smaller item on 9 and 14 February on company and rally catalysts; this item is a material update centred on the GME/AMC divergence (GME +17.88% vs AMC -1.02% over 20 sessions).
considered_not_chosen: Home Depot (-8.85% to 316.17 USD on a margin warning, Reuters n0985, CNN n0725, CNBC n0984): large drop with good coverage, but weaker retail-crowd evidence; Lowe's results are pending on the report date and were not referenced.

Defense (LMT -0.07% to 386.20 USD, just below the 386.46 USD line the 22 February item set; ITA -1.38%; Rheinmetall +2.20%): the war trade did not rally in US defense names on the recognition, but there is no newly published defense-stock evidence, so no carryover.

Bitcoin (+3.27% to 38,286.03 USD while COIN -6.56%, MARA -5.69%, BITO -5.26%) and Coinbase backpedalling over its Super Bowl ad (n0126): crypto already appeared on 2, 4, 7, 8, 9, 14, 15, 18 and 21 February and as backdrop in the 22 February lead; not repeated without a new crowd catalyst.
Wheat (+5.93% to 844.25 US cents/bu; Marketplace n1724): folded into the oil lead as part of the commodity spillover rather than given its own slot.

Avoided as wording or timing risks: n1104 (New York Post headline describing an 'invasion' for the 22 February deployment) is not cited; n1255's 'beginning invasion' is used only as Biden's characterisation, attributed via Al Jazeera, alongside the sanctions it reports, and the Guardian's 'Russia orders troops into Ukraine' (n1263) is attributed to the Guardian. No RBNZ, Lowe's, TJX, Lucid or eBay outcome headlines were used because those events fall on 23 February.

Ford (-4.16% to 17.29 USD): the 22 February Ford item was removed in review because its only support (Los Angeles Times n1030 in that feed) could not be shown to precede the cutoff; there is no new own-date Ford evidence, so Ford is not used.

China internet ETF (KWEB -4.24% to 34.09 USD, below the 35.60 USD line set on 22 February; Alibaba HK -3.05%) and TQQQ (-3.09% to 48.88 USD, the gap risk flagged on 22 February): both 22 February break conditions were met, but there is no newly published crowd evidence, so neither is carried over.
Reuters' 18 February preview that commodity supplies are at risk if Russia is hit by sanctions (n0541) was dropped from the lead in review as superseded by the actual 22 February tranches.
